name: SC-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+21 partisan lean makes it one of the most Republican House seats
Incumbent Sheri Biggs running with a roughly 12-to-1 fundraising advantage
Democrat Eunice Lehmacher minimally funded with no outside spending on either side
Prediction markets price the Republican at about 95 percent
model.rationale: A twenty-point Republican district, an incumbent with a roughly twelve-to-one money advantage, and no visible Democratic infrastructure leave Lehmacher without a credible path, and markets agree the seat is effectively out of reach for Democrats.
model.watch: Only a large, late wave of outside spending against Biggs or an extreme national Democratic environment could narrow the margin, and even that would be unlikely to threaten the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
South Carolina's 3rd District is among the most Republican seats in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly twenty points to the GOP. First-term incumbent Sheri Biggs is seeking re-election after clearing her primary, and she faces Democrat Eunice Lehmacher and Libertarian Brian Corriea in the general election. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the picture rests on fundamentals, money, and market pricing.

The financial gap is stark: Biggs has raised about half a million dollars and holds roughly $219,000 on hand, while Lehmacher has raised about $41,000 with under $18,000 available, and no outside spending has materialized for either side. Prediction markets put the Republican's chances around 95 percent. With the seat's deep Republican lean and an incumbent advantage, Biggs is positioned as a heavy favorite, and the main question is the size of her winning margin rather than the outcome.
